title.zh: 卷三十五 志第五: 兵衞志中
title.raw: 卷三十五 志第五: 兵衞志中 Volume 35 Treatises 5: Military 2

translations.literal: Military Guards, Part 2 ○ Imperial Tent Guard Armies
translations.idiomatic: Military Guards, Part 2 — Imperial Tent Guard Armies

sentences.zh: 漢武帝多行幸之事，置期門、佽飛、羽林之目，天子始有親軍。

translations.literal: Han Emperor Wu often traveled on inspection tours and established the titles Qimen, Cifei, and Yulin; the Son of Heaven first had a personal guard army.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han made many inspection tours and created the Qimen, Cifei, and Yulin corps—the Son of Heaven first gained a personal guard army.

sentences.zh: 唐太宗加親、勛、翊、千牛之衛，布腹心之地，防衛密矣。

translations.literal: Tang Emperor Taizong added the Qin, Xun, Yi, and Qianniu guards, posting them in the heartland; defense became dense indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong of Tang added the Qin, Xun, Yi, and Qianniu guards and stationed them in the imperial core; the protective screen grew tight indeed.

sentences.zh: 遼太祖宗室盛強，分叠剌部為二，宮衛內虛，經營四方，未遑鳩集。

translations.literal: When Liao Taizu rose the imperial clan was strong; he split the Dieci tribe in two, the inner palace guard was hollow, and while he campaigned on four sides he had no leisure to gather forces.
translations.idiomatic: At Liao Taizu's rise the imperial clan was powerful; he divided the Dieci tribe in two, leaving the inner palace guard thin, and while campaigning on every side had no time to muster troops.

sentences.zh: 皇后述律氏居守之際，摘蕃漢精銳為屬珊軍。

translations.literal: While Empress Shulü held the capital, she picked the finest of Fan and Han troops for the shushan army.
translations.idiomatic: While Empress Shulü kept guard at the capital she selected elite Fan and Han troops for the shushan army.

sentences.zh: 太宗益選天下精甲，置諸爪牙為皮室軍。

translations.literal: Taizong further chose the finest armor in the realm and placed them at his claws and teeth as the pishi army.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong further culled the realm's finest armor-bearers and set them at claw and fang as the pishi army.

translations.literal: Together they mustered five hundred thousand horsemen; the state's prestige was majestic.
translations.idiomatic: Combined they fielded five hundred thousand riders; national might stood full and grand.

sentences.zh: 大帳皮室軍：太宗置，凡三十萬騎。

translations.literal: Great-tent pishi army: established by Taizong, altogether three hundred thousand riders.
translations.idiomatic: The great-tent pishi army was Taizong's creation—three hundred thousand riders in all.

sentences.zh: 屬珊軍：地皇后屬，二十萬騎。

translations.literal: Shushan army: belonging to the Earth Empress, two hundred thousand riders.
translations.idiomatic: The shushan army belonged to the Earth Empress and numbered two hundred thousand riders.
Palace-guard cavalry

sentences.zh: 太祖以叠剌部受禪，分本部為五院、六院，統以皇族，而親衛缺然。

translations.literal: Taizu received the mandate through the Dieci tribe, divided the original tribe into Five Courts and Six Courts, and governed them with the imperial clan—yet personal guards were still lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu took the mandate through the Dieci tribe, split the original tribe into Five Courts and Six Courts under imperial-clan control, yet personal guards were still wanting.

sentences.zh: 乃立斡魯朵法，裂州縣，割戶丁，以強幹弱支。

translations.literal: He then established the orudo law, carved up prefectures and counties, and cut off household men to strengthen the trunk and weaken the branches.
translations.idiomatic: He then set up the orudo law, split prefectures and counties, and drew off household men to strengthen the center and weaken the periphery.

translations.literal: Plans were entrusted and achievements inherited; generation after generation palace guards were built.
translations.idiomatic: Plans were handed down and achievements continued; palace guards were raised generation after generation.

sentences.zh: 入則居守，出則扈從，葬則因以守陵。

translations.literal: When within they guarded the residence; when without they escorted on campaign; at burial they accordingly guarded the tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Within they held the capital; abroad they escorted the ruler; at burial they were posted to guard the tombs.

sentences.zh: 有兵事，則五京、二州各提轄司傳檄而集，不待調發州縣、部族，十萬騎軍已立具矣。

translations.literal: When there was war, each supervisory office of the Five Capitals and Two Prefectures transmitted orders and assembled troops; without waiting to mobilize prefectures, counties, or tribes, a hundred thousand riders stood ready.
translations.idiomatic: In time of war each supervisory office of the Five Capitals and Two Prefectures passed orders and gathered troops; without waiting on prefectures, counties, or tribes, a hundred thousand cavalry were already formed.

sentences.zh: 恩意親洽，兵甲犀利，教練完習。

translations.literal: Grace and affection were intimate, weapons and armor sharp, training complete and practiced.
translations.idiomatic: Affection ran close, arms were keen, and drill was thorough and practiced.

sentences.zh: 簡天下精銳，聚之腹心之中。

translations.literal: The finest in the realm were selected and gathered into the belly and heart.
translations.idiomatic: The realm's elite were culled and massed in the imperial core.

sentences.zh: 懷舊者歲深，增新者世盛。

translations.literal: Those cherished from old grew deeper with the years; new additions flourished with each generation.
translations.idiomatic: Old loyalties deepened year by year; new strength waxed with every generation.

translations.literal: This was the excellence of the army system.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the excellence of this army system.

sentences.zh: 弘義宮：正丁一萬六千，蕃漢轉丁一萬四千，騎軍六千。

translations.literal: Hongyi Palace orudo: registered households sixteen thousand, Fan and Han rotating households fourteen thousand, cavalry six thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Hongyi Palace orudo: sixteen thousand registered households (zhengding), fourteen thousand Fan and Han rotating households (zhuanding), and six thousand cavalry.

sentences.zh: 長寧宮：正丁一萬四千，蕃漢轉丁一萬二千，騎軍五千。

translations.literal: Changning Palace orudo: registered households fourteen thousand, Fan and Han rotating households twelve thousand, cavalry five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Changning Palace orudo: fourteen thousand registered households, twelve thousand Fan and Han rotating households, and five thousand cavalry.

sentences.zh: 永興宮：正丁六千，蕃漢轉丁一萬四千，騎軍五千。

translations.literal: Yongxing Palace orudo: registered households six thousand, Fan and Han rotating households fourteen thousand, cavalry five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxing Palace orudo: six thousand registered households, fourteen thousand Fan and Han rotating households, and five thousand cavalry.

sentences.zh: 積慶宮：正丁一萬，蕃漢轉丁一萬六千，騎軍八千。

translations.literal: Jiqing Palace orudo: registered households ten thousand, Fan and Han rotating households sixteen thousand, cavalry eight thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Jiqing Palace orudo: ten thousand registered households, sixteen thousand Fan and Han rotating households, and eight thousand cavalry.

sentences.zh: 延昌宮：正丁二千，蕃漢轉丁六千，騎軍二千。

translations.literal: Yanchang Palace orudo: registered households two thousand, Fan and Han rotating households six thousand, cavalry two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchang Palace orudo: two thousand registered households, six thousand Fan and Han rotating households, and two thousand cavalry.

sentences.zh: 彰湣宮：正丁一萬六千，蕃漢轉丁二萬，騎軍一萬。

translations.literal: Zhangmin Palace orudo: registered households sixteen thousand, Fan and Han rotating households twenty thousand, cavalry ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangmin Palace orudo: sixteen thousand registered households, twenty thousand Fan and Han rotating households, and ten thousand cavalry.

translations.literal: Chongde Palace orudo: registered households twelve thousand, Fan and Han rotating households twenty thousand, cavalry ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Chongde Palace orudo: twelve thousand registered households, twenty thousand Fan and Han rotating households, and ten thousand cavalry.

sentences.zh: 興聖宮：正丁二萬，蕃漢轉丁四萬，騎軍五千。

translations.literal: Xingsheng Palace orudo: registered households twenty thousand, Fan and Han rotating households forty thousand, cavalry five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Xingsheng Palace orudo: twenty thousand registered households, forty thousand Fan and Han rotating households, and five thousand cavalry.

sentences.zh: 延慶宮：正丁一萬四千，蕃漢轉丁二萬，騎軍一萬。

translations.literal: Yanqing Palace orudo: registered households fourteen thousand, Fan and Han rotating households twenty thousand, cavalry ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing Palace orudo: fourteen thousand registered households, twenty thousand Fan and Han rotating households, and ten thousand cavalry.

sentences.zh: 太和宮：正丁二萬，蕃漢轉丁四萬，騎軍一萬五千。

translations.literal: Taihe Palace orudo: registered households twenty thousand, Fan and Han rotating households forty thousand, cavalry fifteen thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Taihe Palace orudo: twenty thousand registered households, forty thousand Fan and Han rotating households, and fifteen thousand cavalry.

sentences.zh: 永昌宮：正丁一萬四千，蕃漢轉丁一萬，騎軍一萬。

translations.literal: Yongchang Palace orudo: registered households fourteen thousand, Fan and Han rotating households ten thousand, cavalry ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yongchang Palace orudo: fourteen thousand registered households, ten thousand Fan and Han rotating households, and ten thousand cavalry.

sentences.zh: 敦睦宮：正丁六千，蕃漢轉丁一萬，騎軍五千。

translations.literal: Dunmu Palace orudo: registered households six thousand, Fan and Han rotating households ten thousand, cavalry five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Dunmu Palace orudo: six thousand registered households, ten thousand Fan and Han rotating households, and five thousand cavalry.

sentences.zh: 文忠王府：正丁一萬，蕃漢轉丁一萬六千，騎兵一萬。

translations.literal: Wenzhong princely establishment: registered households ten thousand, Fan and Han rotating households sixteen thousand, cavalry ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The Wenzhong princely establishment of Yelü Longyun: ten thousand registered households, sixteen thousand Fan and Han rotating households, and ten thousand cavalry.

sentences.zh: 十二宮一府，自上京至南京總要之地，各置提轄司，重地每宮皆置，內地一二而已。

translations.literal: Twelve palaces and one princely establishment, from Shangjing to Nanjing at strategic points, each had a supervisory office set up; in important places every palace had one, in the interior only one or two.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve palace orudo and one princely establishment, from Shangjing to Nanjing at key points, each had a supervisory office; in vital regions every palace had one, inland only one or two.

translations.idiomatic: Taihe and Yongchang should have matched Xingsheng and Yanqing; older histories omit their supervisory offices—probably a gap in the record.

sentences.zh: 凡諸宮衛，丁四十萬八千，出騎軍十萬一千。

translations.literal: In all the palace guards had four hundred eight thousand household men and fielded one hundred one thousand cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: All palace-guard orudo together mustered four hundred eight thousand household men and one hundred one thousand cavalry.
Armies of great chieftains and tribes

sentences.zh: 遼親王大臣，體國如家，征伐之際，往往置私甲以從王事。

translations.literal: Liao imperial princes and great ministers treated the state as their household; on campaigns they often raised private armor to follow the king's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Liao princes and great ministers governed the realm like a household; on campaign they often kept private troops to serve the throne.

sentences.zh: 大者千餘騎，小者數百人，著籍皇府。

translations.literal: The large had more than a thousand riders, the small several hundred, all registered in the imperial registry.
translations.idiomatic: The largest kept over a thousand riders, the smallest several hundred, all entered on the imperial rolls.

sentences.zh: 國有戎政，量借三五千騎，常留餘兵為部族根本。

translations.literal: When the state had military affairs it might borrow three to five thousand riders, always leaving the rest as the tribe's foundation.
translations.idiomatic: In wartime the court might borrow three to five thousand riders while the remainder stayed as each tribe's root force.

sentences.zh: 眾部族軍眾部族分隸南北府，守衛四邊，各有司法，具如左。

translations.literal: Mass tribal armies—mass tribal groups were subordinated to the Northern and Southern Courts, guarding the four borders, each with its own judicial office, as listed at left.
translations.idiomatic: Mass tribal armies: tribal groups were attached to the Northern and Southern Courts to guard the four frontiers, each with its own judicial office, as listed below.
